annotations.description: Mulliganed a 6-card hand with 1 land (Plains), Transcendent Envoy (2-drop), and strong spells including Winged Words (which becomes cheap with the flying Envoy). While 1-land hands are risky, going to 5 cards in Limited is a severe cost. If they draw just 1 land in the first 2 draws, the hand curves out well: T2 Envoy, T3 discounted Winged Words to draw more lands/spells.
annotations.actionTaken: Mulliganed to 5 cards
annotations.betterLine: Keep the 6-card hand. The 1-land hand has a functional curve if even 1 land is drawn, and going to 5 cards is very punishing in Limited.

annotations.description: Thriving Grove's color choice defaulted to White (likely due to timeout) instead of Black. The hand and deck are Black/Green, so choosing White provides no benefit. While current spells can still be cast with Swamp (B) and Grove (G), choosing Black would provide important mana redundancy for future turns, especially for cards like Strangling Spores or additional black spells drawn later.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out, defaulting to White for Thriving Grove's color choice
annotations.betterLine: Choose Black for Thriving Grove, giving access to both Black and Green from the Grove while the Swamp also provides Black, maximizing mana flexibility for the BG deck.

annotations.description: Used Eaten Alive (premium exile removal) on a minor 1/2 Pious Wayfarer instead of developing the board with Ilysian Caryatid. The Caryatid is critical for ramping toward Massacre Wurm (6 mana), which is the strongest card in hand. Wasting exile-quality removal on a 1/2 creature is a significant resource misallocation, and delaying ramp by a turn delays the Wurm substantially.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Eaten Alive targeting Pious Wayfarer, using premium removal on a 1/2 creature.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Ilysian Caryatid to develop mana and accelerate toward Massacre Wurm. The Pious Wayfarer can be dealt with later by Strangling Spores, Savage Punch, or simply blocked by Black Cat.

annotations.description: Failed to attack with Pious Wayfarer into an empty board (opponent's only creature, Ilysian Caryatid, is summoning sick). This was 1 free damage with zero risk.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and did not declare any attackers.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Pious Wayfarer for 1 unblockable damage, then pass to main phase 2 to hold up mana for Nebelgast Herald on opponent's turn.

annotations.description: Timed out and passed the turn without casting Black Cat, the only creature available. With an empty board facing Pious Wayfarer, deploying Black Cat would provide a blocker, enable Eaten Alive as cheap removal later, and begin developing toward casting Massacre Wurm. Wasting 2 mana and missing a key development turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and passed without casting anything, wasting 2 mana.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Black Cat for {1}{B} to establish a board presence, provide a blocker against Pious Wayfarer, and enable future Eaten Alive plays.

annotations.description: Passed with 3 mana available and Chains of Custody castable. Casting Chains of Custody on Pious Wayfarer to exile Black Cat would trigger constellation (+1/+1), give ward {2}, and set up Sage's Reverie next turn for 2 card draws and +2/+2. This establishes the aura synergy engine that the deck is built around.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority in precombat main phase without casting anything
annotations.betterLine: Cast Chains of Custody enchanting Pious Wayfarer, exiling Black Cat. This develops the board (2/3 with ward), removes a blocker, and sets up a powerful Sage's Reverie next turn. Nebelgast Herald could then be held for flash value. Counter-argument: saving Chains for a bigger threat is defensible.

annotations.description: Missed a free attack with Pious Wayfarer for 1 damage. The opponent's only creature (Black Cat 1/1) has summoning sickness and cannot block. There is no downside to attacking here.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and declared no attackers.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Pious Wayfarer for 1 free damage.

annotations.description: Failed to block Pious Wayfarer with Black Cat. Blocking would have resulted in Black Cat dying and triggering a random discard from the opponent, while only costing a 1/1 body. Not blocking preserves the Cat for potential Eaten Alive sacrifice later, but the random discard is likely worth more than the marginal body.
annotations.actionTaken: Did not block (timeout/no response), took 1 damage from Pious Wayfarer
annotations.betterLine: Block Pious Wayfarer with Black Cat to trigger the death trigger for a random discard from the opponent. The 1/1 body has limited future value, and the discard could hit something important from the opponent's 4-card hand.

annotations.description: Passed precombat main without casting Sage's Reverie when opponent has no creatures on board. Casting it precombat on Pious Wayfarer would trigger Constellation, give +1/+1 from the aura, draw a card, and allow a larger attack. With no opposing creatures, there's no reason to delay.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority in precombat main phase without casting any spells
annotations.betterLine: Cast Sage's Reverie on Pious Wayfarer precombat, triggering Constellation for +1/+1, getting +1/+1 from the aura (making it ~3/4), drawing a card, then attacking with the bigger creature

annotations.description: Failed to attack with any creatures when the opponent had zero creatures on the battlefield. Both Nebelgast Herald (2/1 flying) and Pious Wayfarer (1/2) could attack for a free 3 damage with no possible blocks.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and declared no attackers.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Nebelgast Herald and Pious Wayfarer for 3 unblockable damage against an empty board.

annotations.description: Cast Grotesque Mutation with no friendly creatures on the battlefield, meaning it can only target an opponent's attacking creature. This buffs the attacker (+3/+1 and lifelink), causing KimiK2 to take more damage while the opponent gains life. The card is wasted for a negative effect. If the goal was to kill a creature, Strangling Spores alone could handle either attacker without needing the Mutation.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Grotesque Mutation targeting an opponent's attacking creature, buffing it and giving it lifelink.
annotations.betterLine: Do not cast Grotesque Mutation. Either take the 3 damage from both attackers (going to 14), or use Strangling Spores alone to kill one of the attackers. Save Grotesque Mutation for when you have a creature of your own to buff.

annotations.description: Passed the turn in postcombat main with two castable spells available.
